transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Amy Held.
Starting in January, Democrats will control Congress, and Senator Chris Van Hollen of
Maryland says the new party in power must come with new leadership.
He is running to replace Senator Chuck Schumer as Senate Majority Leader.
The scale and scope of this victory, 56 Senate Democratic seats, really gives us a mandate
and the votes to do big things.
But it should be very clear while voters have rejected the Trump policies, they've not yet
hired Democrats.
They've given us a chance.
We have to earn their trust.
Van Hollen speaking to MS Now, he says the voter mandate means a broken economic system
rigged for the wealthy must change.
Schumer, Democratic leader for more than three decades, recruited many of the successful
candidates.
Democrats flipped at least eight seats in the Senate and won more than 250 House races.
This week, more than 100 newly elected lawmakers came to Washington for freshman orientation,
as NPR's Barbara Sprunt reports.
Freshman orientation, often called Congress school, is 10 days long.
The newly elected have a long list of things to learn.
Joe Morelli is the top Democrat on the committee that runs orientation and likely the next
chairman.
Setting up a congressional office, first of all, is like its own small business.
Each of them is different.
They have to do their own hiring.
They have to make decisions on what the scope of each of their staff members could be.
They have to think about legislative procedure.
Coming to Congress means life changes, too.
The incoming freshmen are figuring out their living situation come January.
Some say they'll bunk with other freshmen.
Barbara Sprunt, NPR News.
The European Union says it will send a team of diplomats from across the continent for
Ukraine peace talks.
Till now, negotiations have largely involved just three parties, Moscow, Kiev, and Washington.
Ukraine says it wants more support from its European allies.
President Volodymyr Zelensky has expressed frustration over the U.S.-controlled Starshield
satellite connection being slowed down again, hurting their ability to intercept Russia's
new jet-powered drones.
SpaceX is preparing a critical test launch of its massive Starship rocket today.
And Piers Jeff Brumfield has this report.
Starship is the largest rocket ever built.
It might one day take humans to Mars, but first it's got to make SpaceX a lot of money.
The plan is to use the rocket to launch thousands of Starlink Internet satellites and further
down the line orbital data centers.
The only way Starship can take all this stuff into space is if it can be quickly reused.
To that end, SpaceX intends to fly this test rocket back from orbit to its launch pad in
Texas.
If all goes to plan, it will hover while two mechanical arms on the launch tower catch
it.
Eventually, the company plans to simply gas up the rocket after it's caught and launch
it again.
Jeff Brumfield, NPR News.
It's NPR News.
Parts of the Pacific Northwest are facing flood risk this weekend.
Free rain is forecast in Washington, Oregon, and parts of Northern California, as two atmospheric
rivers drop several inches.
That plus high tides and rising sea levels raise the risk of coastal flooding.
Ocean waters warmed by El Nino are fueling storm systems, and forecasters say part of
Washington's coast could be hit by 20-foot swells.
Meantime, countries are gathered at the COP 31 conference in Turkey.
Most are not on track to reach their climate pledges by transitioning to cleaner energy.
Singers from Argentina and Spain were among the big winners at last night's Latin Grammy
awards.
NPR's Felix Contreras reports the honors were handed out in Las Vegas.
Twenty-year-old Argentine vocalist Milo Hota won Latin Grammys in three different music
categories for his album of Argentine folk music, La Vida Eramar Escorte.
Spanish vocalist Rosalía's genre-defying album, Lux, won the top spots of Album of
the Year, as well as Song of the Year and Best Pop Song.
Recatone pioneer Daddy Yankee was recognized as the Latin Recording Academy's Person
of the Year, which was presented by an unannounced appearance by R&B icon Janet Jackson.
And the newly minted congressman-elect from the Texas 15th congressional district, Bobby
Polido, picked up his third Latin Grammy this year for Best Tejano Album, Felix Contreras,
NPR News.
I'm Amy Held, and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: Sen. Chris Van Hollen says Democrats must change economic system and new leadership, running for Majority Leader
Newly elected House and Senate members begin 10-day freshman orientation in Washington, learning office setup and procedures
European Union plans to send a team of diplomats to join Ukraine peace talks
Zelensky frustrated as slowed Starshield satellite connection hampers interception of Russian jet-powered drones
SpaceX prepares critical test launch of Starship rocket, aiming to catch it back at Texas launch tower
Atmospheric rivers bring flood risk to Washington, Oregon, and Northern California, with 20-foot coastal swells
Countries gather at COP 31 climate conference in Turkey, most off track on clean energy pledges
Latin Grammy winners include Milo Hota, Rosalía, Daddy Yankee honored, and Bobby Pulido's Tejano win
